minutes.headline: Personnel Committee heard SAP staff object to flat-dollar longevity and asked staff to rerun the impact before Town Meeting.
minutes.summary: The committee took up the change of Salary Administration Plan longevity from a percentage to a flat dollar amount. Affected employees objected, and members agreed to ask HR to model examples and report back before the March 15 article deadline. Members also approved a network administrator job description correction, a new part-time assistant to the sewer business manager, and an updated board clerk secretary description. The election worker and registrar positions were deferred.

public_comment.topic: A department head said SAP staff work unpaid extra hours and lack floating holidays the clerical union gets, so losing the percentage longevity feels like a penalty.
An SAP employee seconded those concerns, noted SAP staff have no union rep, and asked not to be equated with the clerical union.
An employee asked whether she is still grandfathered on sick-time buy back.
An employee asked the committee to reconsider the staff longevity change so that nothing is lost.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of December 29th, with two corrections.
Approve the network administrator job description change from non-exempt to exempt.
Approve the job description for assistant to the sewer business manager (grade eight) with the typo corrections.
Approve the updated board clerk secretary job description as amended.

budget_items.what_was_said: Longevity would change from a percentage of salary to a flat dollar amount to match the clerical union, with current recipients held at their present amount until the next level.

budget_items.topic: Financial effect of longevity change on employees
budget_items.what_was_said: HR had not calculated the loss; a percentage rate was estimated and any loss would come after year one. A member asked for sample salaries comparing the two methods.
The part-time position is funded in the sewer enterprise budget for FY22 and is not expected to affect the general fund apart from small indirect costs.
The goal was to pay these roles at minimum wage; the town clerk suggested only the year-round registrar belongs on the SAP.

decisions.decision: Members will not reverse the longevity recommendation that night. HR and the town manager will review it with affected employees and return before Town Meeting.
Staff will model sample salaries under percentage versus flat-dollar longevity to show the financial impact.
A special list serve for SAP employees will be created so they get meeting agendas.
Longevity service milestones should say continuous service, to be fixed in the article wording.
The election worker and registrar descriptions and the article will return at the next meeting within a week or two, ahead of the March 15 submission deadline.

what_happened.line: The committee did not reverse the longevity recommendation; HR and the town manager will review it with affected employees and return before Town Meeting.
Staff will model sample salaries under percentage versus flat-dollar longevity to show the financial effect on Salary Administration Plan employees.
Salary Administration Plan staff objected to moving longevity from a percentage of salary to a flat dollar amount matching the clerical union.
Members voted unanimously to approve the network administrator change to exempt, the new part-time assistant to the sewer business manager, and the board clerk secretary description.
The election worker and registrar descriptions and article were deferred to the next meeting, ahead of the March 15 submission deadline.

why_it_matters: The longevity change would alter how long-serving non-union town employees are paid, and the Town Meeting article carrying it is a vote residents may be asked to take.
The new sewer assistant is funded in the sewer enterprise budget, so it is paid from sewer rates rather than the general fund, apart from small indirect costs.
watch_next: The next Personnel Committee meeting, within a week or two, where the election worker and registrar article returns.
The HR sample-salary comparison of percentage versus flat-dollar longevity, due before the March 15 article deadline.
